Today, I researched the materials, construction methods and software needed to create my LED matrix clock for my Half-Life Hack Club project. I wanted to understand the requirements before starting construction so that I could plan the project properly and ensure that the components would work together.

I investigated the hardware I would need, including an LED matrix display, a suitable microcontroller, connecting wires and a power supply. I also considered designing a 3D-printed enclosure to protect the electronics and give the clock a clean, professional appearance.

I researched how the components would connect and communicate, as well as how the display would receive information from the controller. This helped me understand the basic construction process and identify what I need to prepare before assembling the device.

For the programming, I decided to use AWTRIX NG, an open-source platform for LED matrix displays. I chose it because of its useful features, customisation options and existing documentation. Instead of creating every feature from scratch, I can use its existing functionality and adapt the display to suit my project. This should make development more efficient while helping me improve my programming and electronics skills.

Another benefit of open-source software is that I can explore how existing features work and use community resources to help troubleshoot potential problems.

Overall, this research has helped me develop a clearer plan for my LED matrix clock. I now have a better understanding of the hardware, construction process and programming software required. My next step is to finalise my component list, obtain the materials and begin building and testing the clock.
